title: Create release channels and compatibility policy
notes: MBR-912 had a prior partial commit already on this branch (62c29923, 'MBR-912: add release channel compatibility contract', confirmed an ancestor of HEAD via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`). That commit added a purely descriptive, read-only contract: release/channels/release-channel.v1.schema.json, release/channels/README.md, docs/compatibility/release-channels.md, engine/crates/membrane-protocol/src/release_channel.rs (a data model with only `update_available()`/`is_schema_current()` helpers), plus apps/membrane-hub/src/release-channel.mjs and its test (a pure, side-effect-free projection/renderer, no policy decision). None of that prior work enforced anything: nothing refused an unknown channel, an unsupported schema version, or a downgrade -- it only reported whatever it was given. This task's diff is additive on top of that prior commit; it does not remove or rewrite any of it, and does not touch apps/membrane-hub/** (out of this task's allowed paths -- landed/concurrent lane).

What this task added: engine/crates/membrane-protocol/src/compatibility_policy.rs -- the real fail-closed enforcement point. `evaluate_compatibility(current_version, &RawReleaseDescriptor)` is the one policy function; it takes a candidate release exactly as it would arrive off the wire (four raw, untyped strings/one integer -- deliberately NOT the already-typed ReleaseChannelV1, so 'unknown channel' and 'unknown schemaCompatibility' are genuine runtime-checked refusals rather than inputs the type system already makes unreachable), and refuses (returns Err with every violation collected, not just the first) on: an unknown `channel`; an unsupported `schemaVersion`; an explicitly `unknown` or `incompatible` `schemaCompatibility` (never assumed compatible by default); and a downgrade, using the identical strictly-greater `major.minor.patch` version-triple rule membrane-updater's (MBR-911, engine/crates/membrane-updater/src/lib.rs) `is_upgrade` already enforces for update admission -- reimplemented independently (not imported: membrane-protocol is a lower-layer contract crate and must not depend on membrane-updater; no crate under engine/crates currently depends on membrane-updater) so the two policies cannot silently diverge. `evaluate_release_channel(current_version, &ReleaseChannelV1)` runs an already schema-valid, typed descriptor through the identical function via `RawReleaseDescriptor::from` -- there is exactly one enforcement path, not a separate 'trusted' fast path that could admit something the raw path would refuse. release_channel.rs gained `ReleaseChannel::as_str()`/`SchemaCompatibility::as_str()` (the exact wire strings each enum variant serializes to/from) so that conversion is explicit and typed rather than round-tripped through serde_json.

release/channels/compatibility-policy.mjs is a dependency-free JavaScript mirror of the exact same policy (same four violation codes, same version-triple comparison, same 'proven, not assumed, compatible' rule for schemaCompatibility), living under this task's release/channels/** allowed path. tests/compat/release-channel-compatibility.test.mjs is the one test file this task actually executed: `node --test tests/compat/release-channel-compatibility.test.mjs`, 14/14 pass (see commands.log) -- proving the policy is machine-checkable today, not only documented. The Rust module's #[test]s (12 cases: unknown channel, unsupported schema version, unrecognized/explicit-unknown schemaCompatibility, incompatible schema, downgrade, equal-version, unparseable candidate/current version, multi-violation, compatible-upgrade admit, migration_required admit-and-flag, typed-descriptor wrapper, as_str round trip) are source-verified by type and were NOT executed, per this task's hard rule against running cargo; they are left for `cargo test --manifest-path engine/Cargo.toml --workspace` at the Book 3 final phased gate, exactly like MBR-903's and MBR-911's own #[test] blocks in this same book.

release/channels/README.md and docs/compatibility/release-channels.md were both extended (not rewritten) to name the channel support-window model (stable/beta/nightly, what 'supported' means and when each channel's window closes) and to point at the enforcement functions and their exact test commands, so the documentation states what is verifiably enforced rather than overstating enforcement that does not exist -- consistent with this repository's rule to 'report typed degradation without overstating enforcement.'

Explicitly out of scope and NOT done, honestly: wiring a Hub or CLI call site to actually invoke evaluate_compatibility/evaluateCompatibility before rendering a channel decision. apps/membrane-hub/** is outside this task's allowed paths (already-landed/concurrent lane per this task's hard rules); release/channels/README.md and docs/compatibility/release-channels.md both say so explicitly rather than implying the policy is already wired into a live UI. The dispatch-manifest.json's allowedPaths for MBR-912 lists apps/membrane-hub/** and this task's explicit owner instructions restrict it to release/channels/**, engine/crates/membrane-protocol/**, docs/compatibility/**, tests/compat/**, evidence/productization/MBR-912/** -- the explicit, more specific owner instructions were followed over the more permissive manifest entry, per this task's own stated authority.

No cargo, pnpm, Tauri, right-release, codesign, notarytool, stapler, spctl, signtool, or AzureSignTool command was run. No mutating git command (add/commit/checkout/stash/reset/rebase/push) was run. No .github/workflows/**, CI, or hosted/self-hosted runner configuration was added. No new Cargo.toml dependency was added -- compatibility_policy.rs uses only membrane-protocol's existing `crate::release_channel` items and the Rust standard library (str::split, char::is_ascii_digit); no new crate dependency was declared.
